title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.

hints.h1: Can you check if the complement (target - current_number) has already been seen as you traverse the array?
hints.h2: A Hash Map (dictionary) provides O(1) average lookup time. What should you store as the key, and what as the value?
hints.h3:
Algorithm steps:
1. Initialize an empty hash map `prevMap` mapping value -> index.
2. For each index `i` and number `n` in `nums`:
   a. Calculate `diff = target - n`.
   b. If `diff` exists in `prevMap`, return `[prevMap[diff], i]`.
   c. Otherwise, insert `prevMap[n] = i`.
3. Return empty list if no pair found.
